research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic official-source research confidence only. Current GOV.UK/Defra and Environment Agency material checked on 25 July 2026. Waste planning policy, waste hierarchy, circular-economy strategy, permits, exemptions, public-register data, duty of care, workplace recycling and packaging obligations remain at their published regulatory, policy or operational scope. They are not parcel waste-facility permissions, contamination results, permit-compliance certificates, capacity guarantees or Future Growth score accuracy.

source_facts.fact: Current planning guidance retains the priority order of prevention, preparing for reuse, recycling, other recovery and disposal, and identifies the hierarchy as relevant to waste planning and individual waste-management proposals.
source_facts.gate: The hierarchy is a policy priority and not a site permit, planning permission or waste-capacity result.

source_facts.fact: Environment Agency guidance distinguishes regulatory position statements, exemptions, standard-rules permits and bespoke permits for waste activities.
source_facts.gate: An exemption or RPS is not a planning permission and must be checked against its own conditions and expiry/status.

source_facts.fact: Most waste exemptions must be registered, are conditional and are normally valid for three years from registration; current digital registration rules were updated in 2026.
source_facts.gate: Registration is not evidence that every activity at a site is lawful or compliant.

source_facts.fact: EA public registers provide permit, exemption and carrier/broker/dealer records but explicitly direct users to a separate enforcement-actions register for enforcement history.
source_facts.gate: Public-register presence or absence must not be converted into a complete compliance history.

source_facts.fact: Household rules came into force in England on 31 March 2026, while workplace obligations and producer rules have their own separate scopes and dates.
source_facts.gate: National recycling rules do not establish a parcel's waste infrastructure capacity or planning acceptability.

source_facts.fact: Defra's 2026 circular-economy guidance for mayoral strategic authorities supports circularity in growth and spatial strategies while remaining strategic guidance.
source_facts.gate: Circular-economy policy is not evidence a particular development has achieved reuse/recycling targets.

core_rules: waste hierarchy is a policy priority not a site permit
prevention priority does not prove a development will prevent waste
reuse target or strategy does not prove actual reuse performance
recycling target does not prove site recycling capacity
recovery and disposal must remain distinct waste-management outcomes
waste planning permission is distinct from environmental permit
environmental permit is distinct from planning permission
standard-rules permit eligibility must not be assumed without activity and site checks
bespoke permit requirement must not be inferred solely from land use
permit application is not permit grant
permit grant is not proof ongoing compliance
permit variation application is not approved variation
RPS coverage is conditional and time-limited where stated
RPS is not an environmental permit or planning permission
waste exemption is conditional and not an unrestricted right
waste exemption registration is not proof every activity is exempt
exemption expiry date must be checked before treating registration as current
multiple-site registration does not make every activity at every site compliant
linear-network exemption process is not a linear-infrastructure planning approval
EA public-register record is not a parcel planning decision
absence from public register does not prove no historic permit or enforcement history
enforcement actions require their own register and must not be inferred from permit search
waste carrier registration is not permission to operate a waste facility
duty-of-care compliance is distinct from site permitting
waste transfer note is not evidence waste was lawfully treated at destination
waste classification code is not a contamination measurement
historic waste activity does not prove current waste operation
current waste activity does not prove historic landfill status
deposit-for-recovery permit is not a landfill permit
recovery-plan approval is not planning permission
recovery of waste on land must not be described as beneficial without permit-specific evidence
waste-planning allocation is not an environmental permit
waste-plan policy support is not planning permission
circular-economy strategy is strategic guidance not project certification
mayoral circularity guidance does not establish a parcel reuse score
Simpler Recycling rules do not prove a development has adequate bin storage
household and workplace recycling duties must remain distinct
producer-responsibility obligation is not a planning condition
packaging recycling target is not a building-development target
national recycling statistics must not be downscaled into parcel performance
waste-management infrastructure proximity does not prove capacity availability
waste-facility capacity must not be fabricated without operator or authority evidence
planning policy for waste does not remove nuisance pollution or health controls
waste hierarchy application is context-specific and may require lifecycle evidence
permit compliance does not prove land is uncontaminated
closed waste site does not imply remediated or developable land
NO_DATA must not be converted into no waste constraint or no permit requirement
no parcel waste permission permit compliance capacity result or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
